holder_count is null for every row (Finnhub ownership endpoints are Premium). Options in finnhub_fields.md §4: (A) 13F institutional holders only — label 'Institutional holders (13F)'; (B) 10-K Item 5 holders of record — excludes brokerage/street-name owners — label 'Holders of record (registered)'; (C) omit/null — recommended for M1.
Live price/news/logo/last_quarter fields stay null until finnhub_client fills them with a real FINNHUB_API_KEY.

companies.short_description: NVIDIA makes the graphics chips that power many gaming PCs and the big computers that train AI. If you play on a high-end PC or see AI tools everywhere, NVIDIA is usually behind the scenes.
companies.quarterly_summary: Revenue was $96.2 billion, up 106% from a year ago. Sales of chips for big data centers were $89.0 billion, up 117%, as customers kept buying chips to run AI.
companies.listing_notes: Still listed as of Nov 2026 research.

interests.why_line: You picked Gaming — NVIDIA makes the graphics chips inside many gaming PCs.

companies.short_description: AMD makes processors and graphics chips for PCs, game consoles, and data centers. You may know its Ryzen chips in laptops or Radeon graphics in gaming PCs.
companies.quarterly_summary: Revenue was a record $13.4 billion, up 45% from a year ago. Sales of chips for big data centers nearly doubled to $8.5 billion, while gaming chip sales fell 40%.
companies.listing_notes: Still listed as of Nov 2026 research.

interests.why_line: You picked Gaming — AMD makes the processors and graphics chips inside many gaming PCs and consoles.

companies.short_description: Roblox is a free app where millions of people play games that other players build, and spend real money on Robux, its in-game currency, for outfits and extras.
companies.quarterly_summary: Revenue was $1.6 billion, up 16% from a year ago, but the money players spent on Robux fell 12% and daily players dropped 9% to 138 million, after a huge 2025.
companies.listing_notes: Still listed as of Nov 2026 research.

interests.why_line: You picked Gaming — Roblox is one of the most-played game platforms in the world, especially with teens.

companies.short_description: Take-Two makes popular video games such as Grand Theft Auto, NBA 2K, and Red Dead Redemption. It publishes games for consoles, PCs, and phones.
companies.quarterly_summary: Revenue was $1.53 billion, a bit above the year-ago quarter. The company was still preparing for the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI.
companies.listing_notes: Still listed as of Nov 2026 research.

interests.why_line: You picked Gaming — Take-Two makes hit games like Grand Theft Auto and NBA 2K.

companies.short_description: NetEase makes and runs popular mobile and PC games in China and around the world, including long-running hits and newer titles people play on phones and computers.
companies.quarterly_summary: Revenue was about RMB30.1 billion (about US$4.4 billion), up 7.9% from a year ago. Games brought in about RMB25.0 billion, up 9.7%, as titles like Fantasy Westward Journey and Where Winds Meet kept players spending.
companies.listing_notes: Replaces EA (delisted) per John's decision 2026-11-03; live Finnhub free check passed 2026-11-03.

interests.why_line: You picked Gaming — NetEase makes some of the most-played mobile and PC games in China and beyond.

companies.short_description: Unity makes the software tools many studios use to build video games for phones, PCs, and consoles. If a game feels smooth across devices, Unity may be behind it.
companies.quarterly_summary: Revenue was $547 million, up 24% from a year ago. Unity also sold its Supersonic mobile publishing business to focus on its core game engine and ads tools.
companies.listing_notes: Confirmed trading NYSE:U ~2026-11-03.

interests.why_line: You picked Gaming — Unity makes the game-building tools behind many of the titles people play on phones and consoles.

companies.short_description: Microsoft makes Windows, Office, Xbox, and cloud services many people use at work and at home. Xbox games, Game Pass, and Azure are part of everyday tech for millions.
companies.quarterly_summary: Revenue was $92.3 billion, up 19% from a year ago. Cloud kept growing fast; Xbox content and services sales were down a little, about 2%.
companies.listing_notes: Still listed as of Nov 2026 research.

interests.why_line: You picked Gaming — Microsoft owns Xbox, Game Pass, and a big library of games people play every day.

companies.short_description: Sony makes PlayStation consoles and games, plus headphones, cameras, and entertainment. If you play on a PS5 or listen with Sony earbuds, you already know the brand.
companies.quarterly_summary: PlayStation and related game services brought in about ¥937 billion, roughly flat with a year ago. Profit from that gaming business rose 37%.
companies.listing_notes: US ADR (NYSE:SONY). Price observed ~2026-11-03. Finnhub free US-ticker support expected; live response UNVERIFIED without API key.

interests.why_line: You picked Gaming — Sony makes PlayStation consoles and many of the games people play on them.

companies.short_description: Booking Holdings runs Booking.com, Priceline, and Kayak — websites people use to reserve hotels, flights, and vacation stays around the world.
companies.quarterly_summary: People booked about $54.5 billion of travel through Booking's sites, up 10% from a year ago. Reported sales were $8.89 billion after a one-time cut tied to a U.S. consumer-protection case.
companies.listing_notes: Still listed as of Nov 2026 research.

interests.why_line: You picked Travel — Booking.com and Kayak are where many people find and book hotels and trips.

companies.short_description: Airbnb is the app people use to rent homes, apartments, and unique stays from hosts in cities and vacation spots worldwide.
companies.quarterly_summary: Revenue was $3.61 billion, up 17% from a year ago. Guests booked about 148 million nights and seats, up 10%.
companies.listing_notes: Still listed as of Nov 2026 research.

interests.why_line: You picked Travel — Airbnb is how many people book homes and unique stays instead of a hotel.

companies.short_description: Marriott runs or franchises hotel brands such as Marriott, Courtyard, Westin, and Ritz-Carlton that travelers stay in around the world.
companies.quarterly_summary: Revenue was $7.0 billion, up from $6.5 billion a year ago. Guests paid more per stay on average, and Marriott kept adding hotels.
companies.listing_notes: Still listed as of Nov 2026 research.

interests.why_line: You picked Travel — Marriott hotels like Courtyard, Westin, and Ritz-Carlton are places many people stay on trips.

companies.short_description: Hilton is behind hotel brands such as Hilton, Hampton, DoubleTree, and Embassy Suites that travelers book for business and vacations.
companies.quarterly_summary: Revenue was $3.33 billion, up from $3.12 billion a year ago. Guests paid more per stay on average, and Hilton kept adding hotels.
companies.listing_notes: Still listed as of Nov 2026 research.

interests.why_line: You picked Travel — Hilton hotels like Hampton and DoubleTree are common stays for trips and work travel.

companies.short_description: Delta is a major U.S. airline people fly for trips across the country and overseas. Its hubs include Atlanta, New York, and Los Angeles.
companies.quarterly_summary: Revenue was $17.6 billion, up about 16% from a year ago. Higher ticket prices and strong demand helped cover much higher fuel costs.
companies.listing_notes: Still listed as of Nov 2026 research.

interests.why_line: You picked Travel — Delta is one of the big airlines people fly for vacations and visits.

companies.short_description: Southwest is a popular U.S. airline known for domestic flights and a more casual boarding style. Many people use it for city-to-city trips.
companies.quarterly_summary: Operating revenue hit a company third-quarter record of $8.4 billion, up 21.2% from a year ago. Travelers paid more per trip even as fuel costs jumped.
companies.listing_notes: Still listed as of Nov 2026 research.

interests.why_line: You picked Travel — Southwest is a go-to airline for many people flying around the U.S.

companies.short_description: Expedia Group runs Expedia, Hotels.com, and Vrbo — apps and sites people use to book flights, hotels, and vacation rentals.
companies.quarterly_summary: Revenue was $4.32 billion, up 14% from a year ago. The total value of trips people booked rose 12%.
companies.listing_notes: Still listed as of Nov 2026 research.

interests.why_line: You picked Travel — Expedia, Hotels.com, and Vrbo are tools many people use to plan and book trips.

companies.short_description: Uber is the app people open for rides across town and for food delivery. It also helps move freight for businesses.
companies.quarterly_summary: Revenue was $14.2 billion, up 12% from a year ago. Rides and food delivery stayed the main ways people use Uber day to day.
companies.listing_notes: Still listed as of Nov 2026 research.

interests.why_line: You picked Travel — Uber is how many people get around cities when they visit somewhere new.

companies.short_description: Live Nation puts on concerts worldwide and owns Ticketmaster, the ticketing site many people use to buy seats for shows.
companies.quarterly_summary: Revenue was $7.7 billion, up 9% from a year ago. About 49 million fans attended its shows, up 10%.
companies.listing_notes: Still listed as of Nov 2026 research.

interests.why_line: You picked Music — Live Nation and Ticketmaster are behind many of the concerts people go to.

companies.short_description: Spotify is the streaming app millions use to listen to music, podcasts, and audiobooks on phones and speakers.
companies.quarterly_summary: Revenue rose 16% from a year ago to about €5.0 billion. Paid Premium subscribers reached 306 million.
companies.listing_notes: Still listed as of Nov 2026 research.

interests.why_line: You picked Music — Spotify is one of the main apps people open to stream songs and podcasts.

companies.short_description: Warner Music is a major record company behind artists and song catalogs people hear on streaming apps, radio, and in movies.
companies.quarterly_summary: Revenue was $1.86 billion, up 10.4% from a year ago. Both recorded music and song publishing helped the gain.
companies.listing_notes: Confirmed still trading NASDAQ:WMG ~2026-11-03.

interests.why_line: You picked Music — Warner Music works with many of the artists whose songs fill playlists and charts.

companies.short_description: Apple makes the iPhone, Mac, and AirPods, and runs Apple Music, where people stream songs and playlists on their devices.
companies.quarterly_summary: Revenue was $114.5 billion, up 12% from a year ago. Services, which include Apple Music, hit an all-time high of about $31.6 billion.
companies.listing_notes: Still listed as of Nov 2026 research. Music via Apple Music / services.

interests.why_line: You picked Music — Apple Music is one of the big ways people stream songs on iPhones and other devices.

companies.short_description: Amazon is the online store and Prime Video/Amazon Music company many people shop and stream with. Alexa speakers and Kindle sit in lots of homes too.
companies.quarterly_summary: Sales were $201.9 billion, up 12% from a year ago. Amazon's cloud business, AWS, jumped 39% to about $46 billion.
companies.listing_notes: Still listed as of Nov 2026 research. Music via Amazon Music / devices.

interests.why_line: You picked Music — Amazon Music and Alexa are how many people stream songs at home and on the go.

companies.short_description: Sirius XM is the satellite and streaming audio service many people listen to in the car for music, sports talk, and podcasts.
companies.quarterly_summary: Revenue was $2.15 billion, down slightly from a year ago. Profit rose 7% to $317 million.
companies.listing_notes: Post–Liberty Media split-off/merger (Sep 2024) still trades as NASDAQ:SIRI.

interests.why_line: You picked Music — Sirius XM is the audio many people hear in the car for music and talk shows.
